newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity continues higher with natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity continues higher with natgas.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) rose again Tuesday, taking their cue from higher natural gas prices in the region, industry sources said.
"I think (the rise) is primarily due to the panic in the natgas market," one power marketer said.

Natural gas prices in Texas rose again Tuesday after a jump Monday on production cuts in preparation for Tropical Storm Josephine. Gas operations returned to near normal Tuesday as the storm was downgraded and continued north.
Also, startup of Lower Colorado River Authority's 430 megawatt (MW) Ferguson gas plant was postponed to October 9 from original estimates the plant would resume service today.
On-peak firm ERCOT power for Tuesday delivery was talked at $21.00-23.00 from $20.00-22.50 on Monday, the sources said.
Off-peak firm next-day power was said to be talked higher near $12.00-14.00 from a range of $10.00-14.00 on Monday.
November ERCOT power was also talked higher at $19.50-20.50 from a range of $19.50-20.00 on Monday, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
